items.title: Introducing Sysdig AI Defense: See, stop, and prove what agents do
items.summary: Sysdig AI Defense is runtime security and governance for every AI agent your teams run, from the laptop where an agent starts its work to the cloud where its actions land. It starts by showing you what’s there. It finds the agents, MCP servers, skills and plugins your people use, including the ones nobody approved, and ties each one to the account and the person behind it.

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619): Detecting unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP core
items.summary: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on a PHP server with HTTP requests alone. The Sysdig Threat Research Team analyzed the exploitation and outlines affected versions, mitigations, and how to detect post-exploitation activity at runtime with Sysdig Secure and open source Falco.

items.summary: An AI agent once deleted someone's entire inbox despite being told to confirm first. Not because it was malicious, but because the instruction didn't survive context compaction. Shantanu Gattani, Sysdig's SVP of Product, on why that gap is the real risk in agentic AI, and who should be responsible for closing it.
